newsitem.title: USA: NeoPharm drug to be reviewed by FDA.
newsitem.headline: NeoPharm drug to be reviewed by FDA.

text.p: NeoPharm Inc said Monday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has accepted for review the company's New Drug Application covering use of broxuridine, a drug to predict a patient's survival and potential tumor recurrence in breast cancer.

After a preliminary review, the FDA also said that the company's application to use broxuridine as a radiation sensitizer in the treatment of malignant brain tumors, is not sufficiently complete to permit a substantive review at this time, NeoPharm said.

NeoPharm said it has requested a meeting with the FDA to discuss issues raised in its review of the malignant brain tumor indication. The company said it believes that if it submits additional supportive data it could satisfy the requirements of the FDA for this indication.
The NDA covering both indications was filed in December, 1996. About 180,000 new cases of breast cancer and 15,000 new cases of brain cancer are reported each year in the U.S.
William C. Govier, M.D., Ph.D., president and chief executive officer said, "The acceptance of the breast cancer NDA for review represents an important milestone in the company's development.
NeoPharm said it is also evaluating clinical data for other possible applications of broxuridine in both therapeutic and diagnostic indications.
